_meta.source: Every point resolved individually against OpenStreetMap on 31 July 2026 by Nominatim search, with an Overpass sweep of the Takoradi harbour and Market Circle area. None is estimated. The port pin is an OSM-mapped pier inside the commercial harbour where the General Multipurpose Berths lie; no berth-level detail is published and none is invented. The map opens on the berth and its own district because that is where the short-drive options are, and because at any zoom showing Cape Coast 81 km east the whole Takoradi cluster collapses into one marker.

port_pin.label: Takoradi Harbour — the General Multipurpose Berths

bbox_hint.note: Takoradi is on Ghana's Western Region coast. The port day runs east along the coast: Shama at 20 km, Cape Coast at 81 km, Elmina 15 minutes beyond it, and Kakum 30 km inland from there.

fit.why: The port day spans 81 km east while the berth and Market Circle are 1.9 km apart, and no single view holds both legibly — measured at 8 px separation when the box was stretched to Cape Coast. The map therefore opens on what is actually near: the berth, Market Circle, Fort Orange at Sekondi and Fort San Sebastian at Shama, which is the page central finding — a component of the same World Heritage property 20 km away. Cape Coast, Elmina, Kakum, Busua, Axim and Nzulezo are all on the map and appear one zoom out, and the map intro says so.

pois.name: Market Circle
pois.notes: Takoradi's circular central market and the town's own landmark, about 1.5 km from the harbour gate. The nearest thing to a walk-off attraction — subject to whether the port enclosure permits walking out, which is unresolved.

pois.name: Fort Orange, Sekondi
pois.notes: A Dutch fort of 1642 in the twin town of Sekondi, now functioning as a lighthouse. A component of the 1979 UNESCO inscription Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions. Whether it admits visitors at all, given the lighthouse function, is unverified.

pois.name: Fort San Sebastian, Shama
pois.notes: Portuguese, from the 1520s — sources give 1523 and 1526 — and one of the oldest European forts in sub-Saharan Africa. About 20 km east of Sekondi-Takoradi, and a component of the same 1979 World Heritage inscription as Cape Coast and Elmina. The honest alternative for anyone who cannot commit to the 81 km run.

pois.name: Cape Coast Castle
pois.notes: Built by the Swedes in 1653 as Carolusburg and in British hands from 1664, later the headquarters of British administration on the Gold Coast. The male and female dungeons, and the Door of No Return. 81 km east of Takoradi, about 1 h 12 min each way. Entry GH₵80 for a non-Ghanaian adult; hours widely given as 09:00–17:00 daily, though the Ghana Museums and Monuments Board publishes fees without hours.

pois.name: Elmina Castle (St George's)
pois.notes: Founded by the Portuguese in 1482 — the first European trading post on the Gulf of Guinea and the oldest European building still standing south of the Sahara. Dutch from 1637, reconstructed 1770–75. The condemned cell and the export gate. About 15 minutes' drive from Cape Coast Castle; same GH₵80 entry. The town's fishing harbour, packed with painted wooden canoes, is immediately below the walls — Elmina has worked this water since before the fort was built.

pois.name: Kakum National Park
pois.notes: Rainforest reserve with a canopy walkway of seven suspension bridges spanning 350 m, reached by a 20-minute uphill forest walk. Open daily 06:00 to dusk; GH₵130 for a foreign visitor on the walkway, with a gate fee reported at GH₵35 as of October 2025. It lies 30 km beyond Cape Coast, so pairing it with the castles means roughly 220 km of driving.

pois.name: Busua Beach
pois.notes: The Western Region's beach, about 30 km west of Takoradi in the Ahanta West district. Fort Metal Cross at Dixcove — British, from the 1690s, and another component of the same 1979 UNESCO inscription — stands immediately alongside it, which makes a beach day a heritage day as well.

pois.name: Nzulezo
pois.notes: The stilt village on Lake Tadane near Beyin, about 90 km west and reached by canoe. A full day in its own right and not a realistic pairing with anything else on a port call — listed here so that the distance is visible rather than guessed at.

pois.name: Axim
pois.notes: A coastal town about 65 km west of Takoradi, and the site of Fort Saint Anthony — Portuguese, and another of the fifteen forts covered by the 1979 UNESCO inscription that also covers Cape Coast and Elmina. Listed here to show how far the inscribed chain runs: this coast carries fortifications from Keta in the east to Beyin in the west. Coordinates are the gazetteer point for the town; the fort stands on the headland within it.

pois.name: Beyin
pois.notes: The western end of the World Heritage chain. UNESCO describes the 1979 inscription as covering fortified trading posts "between Keta and Beyin", and Fort Apollonia — British, 1770s — stands here. About 90 km west of Takoradi, and the departure point for the canoe to Nzulezo. Listed to show the true extent of the property that Cape Coast and Elmina belong to; the coordinates are the gazetteer point for the village.
